summary: Session-D Next.js (port 3001) consumer-pages migration tested. SSR pages (PDP, Store) + Cart + Wishlist + Buy-now → Checkout sign-in gate + next/image + SEO all PASS. However a CRITICAL config bug makes 70% of the client-fetched flows (Home carousels, /stores, /categories, /c/[slug], /search, /orders/[id], /returns/[id], /account OTP login) unusable when the app is loaded at http://localhost:3001 — the axios client is hard-pointed at the absolute preview URL which serves an invalid CORS preflight (Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true), so every browser XHR is blocked. The fix is one line in api-client.ts (use the Next.js /api rewrite proxy instead of an absolute base URL).

critical.issue: Returns 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' together with 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This combination is rejected by every modern browser whenever the request is sent with credentials:'include' (which the Next.js axios client does). Either echo the request Origin or strip the credentials header server-side.

ui_bugs.issue: baseURL is set to process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL (absolute https://lokl-returns-dash.preview.emergentagent.com). All consumer pages that fetch client-side (Home rails, Stores, Categories, /c/[slug], Search, Orders, Returns, Account) make cross-origin XHRs that the preview ingress's invalid CORS response then blocks. Should be baseURL: '' (relative) so the existing /api/:path* rewrite in next.config.ts handles it.

Hydration mismatch — page logs 'Minified React error #418 (Hydration failed because the server-rendered HTML didn't match the client)'. Functionally still works but throws an error overlay in dev and is a perf/SEO red flag.

integration_issues.issue: All XHRs to /api/* fail with 'CORS preflight … the value of the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header must not be the wildcard * when credentials mode is include'. rca of the issue: Root cause: /app/frontend-next/src/lib/api-client.ts line 140 sets `const baseURL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? "";`. With NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL set to the absolute preview host, every browser XHR from http://localhost:3001 becomes cross-origin. The preview ingress responds with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` plus `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, which the CORS spec forbids — the browser blocks the request and the data layer never resolves. SSR pages (/product, /store) work because they go through `serverFetch` (server-side, no browser, no CORS). The Next.js config (next.config.ts) already declares a /api/:path* rewrite that would have routed the call same-origin through the Next server — but it is bypassed because the axios client uses an absolute base URL. Fix: set api-client baseURL to '' so /api/... is sent relative and the rewrite handles it. Verified reproduction: curl -sI -H 'Origin: http://localhost:3001' https://lokl-returns-dash.preview.emergentagent.com/api/heartbeat → returns access-control-allow-origin: * and access-control-allow-credentials: true (invalid combo). Browser console shows 'Access to XMLHttpRequest … blocked by CORS policy' for every /api endpoint.
